posts.title: Where urushi comes from
posts.excerpt: One tree gives about a cupful of sap in a whole summer. Here is how it is gathered.
posts.content:
From June to October the tapper cuts a thin line across the bark every four days, and a grey milk beads along it. It is scraped into a small wooden pail.

The sap turns brown in the air and black when it cures. We buy it raw from a grove two valleys away and filter it through paper ourselves.

posts.title: Mending a forty-year-old bowl
posts.excerpt: A soup bowl from 1984 came back with a crack in the rim. Six weeks later it went home again.
posts.content:
We cleaned the crack, filled it with lacquer thickened with rice paste and let it cure for a week. Then came three thin undercoats, sanded flat.

Last, two coats of vermilion over the whole rim, so the mend disappears. Its owner says the bowl feels lighter than before.

posts.title: Our stall at the autumn craft fair
posts.excerpt: Two days under the ginkgo trees by the river, with bowls, trays and a box of seconds.
posts.content:
We will be at stall 14 on the second weekend of November, from ten until the light goes. Bring an old piece if you want us to look at it.

The box of seconds has bowls with a speck of dust in the top coat. They work just as well and cost half.
